A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Secant Line Search for Frank-Wolfe Algorithms. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated experimental material.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments in Section 4 and Appendix B, plus secant-versus-Newton timing experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and renumbered Appendices B and C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 retains the same secant updates, clipping, gradient reuse, and stopping rule; warm-starting and fallback strategies also remain unchanged. New Algorithm 3 formalizes inexact Frank-Wolfe for theoretical analysis rather than revising SLS.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight optimization problem classes, standalone root-finding and line-search instances, and standard Frank-Wolfe examples. The experimental appendices are retained under different letters.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Adaptive, Agnostic, Backtracking, Golden Ratio, Monotonic, and Adaptive Zero. The separate Newton comparison and reported Brent comparison are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Instance counts, dimensions, algorithm variants, accuracy settings, and the 10^-7 FW-gap stopping criterion are unchanged. The newly explicit one-hour limit documents the existing experiments rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The secant-versus-Newton tests, step-size trajectories, inner-iteration analysis, and standard Frank-Wolfe checks are retained. No experimental sensitivity or robustness study accompanies the new theoretical precision analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 1000 repetitions for the standalone timing tests and the same averaging conventions. Neither adds seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical results, and the plotted trajectories are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports nuclear-problem times of 204.6 seconds for Secant and 600.6 seconds for Adaptive in both versions.

T1.justification: New Appendix A introduces an inexact-line-search formulation, a weighted primal-dual bound, and derivations connecting accumulated line-search error to outer convergence, with constant and varying accuracy choices. Lemma 2.1 also explicitly states that successive iterate differences converge to zero.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about SLS applicability, adaptivity, computational efficiency, and convergence guarantees. The additional precision analysis does not redefine the headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly discusses how a fixed inner error contributes O(tδ) to its bound and how tolerances should depend on the desired outer accuracy. Existing explanations of numerical instability, warm-starting, and comparator performance remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly specifies a one-hour time limit and states that the experimental implementation is available within FrankWolfe.jl. Existing implementation safeguards, initialization details, and timing procedures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to adaptive step sizes, Newton, Brent, and other Frank-Wolfe strategies are unchanged. Bibliographic formatting and URL spelling changes do not introduce new references or relationships.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely preserved, with local explanations, typo corrections, and author-order/contact updates. The new precision appendix precedes the existing experimental appendices, which become B and C.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 exchange numbering and placement; the step-size panels expand from one column to full width, and the inner-iteration plot is enlarged. Tables 1 and 2 move, while their contents and the remaining experimental graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful precision discussion, reproducibility disclosures, and more legible plots. However, new Appendix A prints an incorrect smoothness inequality, and Algorithm 3 minimizes its linear oracle over R^n rather than the feasible set X. It also does not explicitly connect its objective-error tolerances to Algorithm 2's derivative stopping test. These issues leave the net quality benefit of the main theoretical addition unclear; the empirical evidence is unchanged.
